capabilities: Sort file explorer entries by the numeric value of Arabic, Chinese, and Roman numerals
Handle multi-level numbering, dates, durations, and measure-word numerals in file names
Adjudicate ambiguous numeral segments against the whole folder before sorting
Re-sort on demand via a command or ribbon icon and diagnose ordering in the console
Step aside when the explorer is switched to modified/created time ordering
disambiguation: Not a file renamer; it only changes the display order in the file explorer and leaves names and content untouched.
extras: The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. The README documents deliberate limits (no heavenly-stem/semantic ordering, no fractions, uppercase Roman only) and known misjudgments for numeral idioms like 七七八八, plus a note that v1.0 broke virtual scrolling and v1.1+ is required. Install via BRAT is also supported.
intentEvidence: This plugin replaces the explorer's own sort routine so numbers — Arabic, Chinese and Roman alike — are compared by value
motivation: The author explains that a single misjudged numeral demotes the whole name to text and falls back to pinyin ordering, scrambling the entire list, so v2.0 replaced if-branch guessing with a segment-score-adjudicate pipeline.
problem: Obsidian's file explorer sorts by Unicode code points, so Chinese numerals come out shuffled because their pinyin readings bear no relation to their numeric value.
summary: Chinese-numeral-aware natural sort for the file explorer that orders 第一章/第二章/第十章, Roman and Arabic numerals by value without renaming files.
